provenance.calibration_rationale: Grounded in reference; starting point for the derivation, without which nothing follows. Not empirically tested.

items.title: Field decomposition
items.description: The response writes the total fields as the sum of incident and scattered waves, E = E₀ + E′ and H = H₀ + H′.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step in deriving the scattered-field equations; grounded in reference but not empirically tested.

items.title: Incident-field background equations
items.description: The response writes Maxwell's equations satisfied by the incident fields E₀ and H₀ in the uniform medium with dielectric constant ε₀, separate from the scattered-field equations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference_only: reference writes the incident wave as satisfying its own Maxwell system with ε₀ (equations 3), which is then subtracted from the total-field system.
provenance.discriminates: Response that decomposes the field but does not explicitly state the equations the incident field satisfies in the uniform background.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00; useful context but a near-duplicate precondition. Kept at Optional.

validation.gold_why: Incident-field Maxwell equations written with ε₀.

items.title: Linearization explicit
items.description: The response explicitly states that products of small quantities—specifically δε multiplied by the scattered field E′—are second-order and are neglected in the linear approximation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct finding: all rollouts agreed that δε·E' is O(δε²) and is discarded, leaving source proportional to δε·E₀ only.
provenance.discriminates: Response that retains δε·E' in the scattered-field equation, producing a self-consistent (Born-iterated) rather than first-order linearized problem.

tool_critic.evidence: original validation showed gold_pass=true, discrimination=0.5 with one negative failing; not independently tested via execute_criterion due to tool budget

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; the core approximation the problem asks for, load-bearing for correctness.

validation.gold_why: States neglecting products of small quantities E', H', δε.

items.title: Small-intensity justification
items.description: The response states that the intensity of the scattered field is small compared with that of the incident wave, which justifies neglecting second-order terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference_only: reference explicitly states 'the intensity of the scattered field is small compared with that of the incident wave' as the physical basis for the linearization.
provenance.discriminates: Response that performs the algebraic linearization without stating the physical justification that scattered intensity ≪ incident intensity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; caught both flawed responses, providing the physical reason for the approximation.

validation.gold_why: States scattered intensity is small vs incident wave.

items.title: Scattered-field source equations
items.description: The response writes the scattered-field Maxwell's equations with the source term (4π/c) ∂(δP)/∂t appearing on the right-hand side of curl H′ − (ε₀/c) ∂E′/∂t.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Grounded in reference; the central derived result linking non-uniformity to equivalent sources.

items.title: Polarization uses incident field
items.description: The response states that the induced polarization is δP = (E₀/4π) δε, proportional to the incident field E₀ and δε, not to the total field E or the scattered field E′.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong field in source': identifies mistake of writing δP ∝ δε·E or δε·E' instead of δP ∝ δε·E₀; verified as high-severity and discriminative.
provenance.discriminates: Response that uses the total field E or scattered field E' in the source term, making the source self-consistent (Born-iterated) rather than first-Born.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion confirmed reference passes; original validation showed discrimination=0.5 with one negative failing

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50, pitfall-tested; using the wrong field here breaks the entire derivation.

validation.gold_why: δP = (E₀/4π)δε uses incident field E₀.

items.title: Vibrating dipoles identified
items.description: The response identifies the additional sources as vibrating dipoles distributed in the medium, stating that each volume element dV has dipole moment δP·dV, and that this additional radiation is the scattered light.

provenance.evidence_detail: Verified finding: reference identifies source as distribution of dipoles with moment δP·dV per volume element; counterexample_missing_step showed this is discriminative.
provenance.discriminates: Response that performs the linearization correctly but never explicitly identifies the source as vibrating dipoles with moment proportional to E₀·δε per volume element.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion: reference=true, counterexample_missing_step=false, counterexample_overconfident_incomplete=true, rollout_1=true

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; directly answers the first sub-question's required conclusion about dipole sources.

validation.gold_why: States each dV has dipole moment δP·dV.

items.title: Uniform-medium conclusion
items.description: The response states that the medium can be regarded as uniform with dielectric constant ε₀, with the effect of the non-uniformities equivalent to additional wave sources.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Main thesis of the first sub-question; grounded in reference. Correctness collapses without it.

items.title: Superposition stated
items.description: The response states that when δε is written as Σ δᵢε, the total scattered field is obtained by simple superposition of the fields scattered at each individual non-uniformity δᵢε.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target: explicit superposition statement E' = Σ E'_i; verified finding confirmed counterexample_overconfident_incomplete (omitting part b) is caught by this.
provenance.discriminates: Response that derives the linearized equation but never addresses the decomposition δε = Σ δ_i ε or the consequent superposition of scattered fields.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion: reference=true, counterexample_overconfident_incomplete=false

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; directly answers the second sub-question's requested result.

validation.gold_why: Superposition follows from linearity and homogeneity of system.

items.title: Superposition justification
items.description: The response justifies the superposition result by stating that the scattered-field system is linear and homogeneous with respect to both the fields E′, H′ and to δε.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference_only finding: reference states 'linearity and homogeneity of system (4) with respect both to the fields E', H' and to δε'; rollouts cited only 'linearity of wave operator' which is less precise.
provenance.discriminates: Response that invokes generic 'linearity' without specifying that the system is linear and homogeneous in both the scattered fields and the perturbation δε.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion: reference=true, counterexample_overconfident_incomplete=false; original validation discrimination=1.0

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; caught both flawed responses. The reasoning that makes superposition rigorous.

validation.gold_why: Justifies via linearity and homogeneity in fields and δε.

items.title: Divergence equations written
items.description: The response writes the divergence equations for the scattered field, div(ε₀E′) = −4π div(δP) and div H′ = 0, as part of the scattered-field system.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Grounded in reference; supplementary completeness of the scattered-field equations. Low priority.

items.title: Probability current vanishes
items.description: States that the probability current density vanishes as J = (ℏ/2mi)[ψ*ψ′ − ψ(ψ*)′] = 0 for a real wave function ψ, since ψ* = ψ makes the two terms cancel.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) target: show probability current density j = 0 for real ψ, implying bound state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses Re(ψ*ψ′) instead of Im(ψ*ψ′) would obtain nonzero current and could not conclude J = 0.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion: reference/counterexample_missing_step/negative_constructed1 all pass, but candidate validation metadata reports 0.5 discrimination with one negative failing — negative_constructed2

provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational result with 0.50 discrimination; entire bound-state argument depends on it.

validation.gold_why: States J=0 with the full formula.

items.title: Bound state interpretation
items.description: Connects the vanishing probability current density to the interpretation of the state as bound, i.e., that J = 0 agrees with no net probability flow.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required conceptual link between vanishing current and bound-state characterization; no measured discrimination but necessary.

items.title: Momentum expectation integral
items.description: Writes the momentum expectation value as ⟨ψ|p|ψ⟩ = −iℏ∫_{−∞}^{+∞} ψ(x)ψ′(x) dx, using the position-representation form of the momentum operator.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate setup for the vanishing-momentum proof; 0 discrimination but essential derivation step.

items.title: Total derivative recognition
items.description: Recognizes that ψ(x)ψ′(x) = (1/2) d(ψ²)/dx, converting the momentum integrand into a total derivative.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key algebraic step enabling the boundary evaluation; without it the vanishing-momentum argument fails.

items.title: Boundary term vanishes
items.description: Evaluates the boundary term [ψ²(x)]_{−∞}^{+∞} = 0, using that the bound-state wave function vanishes at ±∞.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Correctness collapses without the vanishing boundary condition; 0 discrimination but physically necessary.

items.title: Zero momentum result
items.description: Concludes that ⟨p⟩_ψ = 0 for the real bound-state wave function, i.e., the state is characterized by vanishing momentum.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary requested result for the first sub-question; correctness anchor for the derivation.

items.title: Chi momentum integral setup
items.description: Writes ⟨χ|p|χ⟩ = −iℏ∫_{−∞}^{+∞} e^{−ip₀x/ℏ}ψ(x) · d/dx[e^{ip₀x/ℏ}ψ(x)] dx, setting up the expectation value for the multiplied state.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate form connecting χ to the momentum computation; 0 discrimination but structurally necessary.

items.title: Decomposition into p₀ + ⟨p⟩_ψ
items.description: Decomposes ⟨p⟩_χ = p₀ + ⟨p⟩_ψ, showing the result combines p₀ with the vanishing momentum of the original bound state.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer writes ⟨p⟩_χ = ⟨p⟩_ψ + p₀ = p₀ as an intermediate decomposition; rollouts computed the two terms separately without this labeling.
provenance.discriminates: A response that arrives at p₀ without connecting it to the previously established ⟨p⟩_ψ = 0 misses the logical link between parts (b) and (c).

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion: reference and negative_constructed1 both pass

provenance.calibration_rationale: Links the two sub-questions; 0 discrimination since both flawed responses got this right, but important reasoning.

validation.gold_why: Writes ⟨p⟩_χ = ⟨p⟩_ψ + p₀.

items.title: Momentum p₀ result
items.description: Concludes that ⟨p⟩_χ = p₀ for the state χ(x) = e^{ip₀x/ℏ}ψ(x), assuming the wave function is normalized.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary requested result for the multiplication sub-question; correctness anchor.

items.title: Normalization assumption
items.description: States or uses that the wave function has been assumed to be normalized, so that ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = 1 enters the momentum calculation.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Real assumption mentioned in the reference; minor weight since it is a stated modelling assumption.

items.title: Fourier transform convention
items.description: Writes the momentum-space wave function as χ̃(p) = (2πℏ)^{−1/2}∫e^{−ipx/ℏ}χ(x) dx with the standard Fourier convention.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) requires studying the problem in the momentum representation via Fourier transform.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips the Fourier transform entirely cannot establish the momentum-space shift.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0 discrimination but required setup for the momentum-representation sub-question; standard formula.

validation.gold_why: Writes Fourier transform with convention.

items.title: Combined Fourier exponent
items.description: Combines the Fourier kernel e^{−ipx/ℏ} with the phase factor e^{ip₀x/ℏ} from χ(x) to obtain the combined exponent e^{−i(p−p₀)x/ℏ} inside the integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: Verified finding: sympy confirmed -ipx/ℏ + ip₀x/ℏ = -i(p-p₀)x/ℏ, establishing the correct minus sign before p₀.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mishandles the sign combination would obtain e^{-i(p+p₀)x/ℏ}, leading to the wrong shift direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 measured discrimination; directly testable and key intermediate for the translation result.

validation.gold_why: Combines exponents to get e^{i(p-p₀)x/ℏ}.

items.title: Momentum-space translation
items.description: States the final result χ̃(p) = ψ̃(p − p₀), i.e., the corresponding momentum wave function is translated in momentum by p₀.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) target: χ̃(p) = ψ̃(p - p₀).
provenance.discriminates: A response writing ψ̃(p + p₀) or ψ̃(p₀ - p) has the shift direction wrong.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary requested result with 0.50 discrimination; correctness anchor for the momentum-representation sub-question.

validation.gold_why: States χ̃(p) = ψ̃(p-p₀).

items.title: Canonical thermal average
items.description: The response writes the canonical thermal average of a physical quantity A as ⟨A⟩_C = Tr(A e^{−βH})/Z_N or the equivalent sum over microstates, for fixed particle number N.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested by the question; no derivation is possible without the canonical average expression.

items.title: Grand canonical average
items.description: The response writes the grand canonical thermal average of A as ⟨A⟩_GC = Tr(A e^{−β(H−μN)})/Ξ or the equivalent sum over states with variable N, where μ is the chemical potential and Ξ is the grand partition function.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested; the grand canonical ensemble average is the counterpart required for the equivalence discussion.

items.title: Grand partition function
items.description: The response expresses the grand partition function in the form Ξ = Σ_N Z_N e^{βμN}, connecting the grand canonical partition function to the canonical partition functions at each N.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question

tool_critic.evidence: Not directly tested via execute_criterion (tool timeouts); validation table reports gold_pass=false, n_negatives_failed=2

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; gold=FAIL but the formula is a load-bearing intermediate connecting the two ensembles.

validation.gold_why: Ξ not expressed as sum of Z_N.

items.title: Weighted canonical sum
items.description: The response states that the grand canonical average can be written as ⟨A⟩_GC = Σ_N (Z_N e^{βμN}/Ξ) ⟨A⟩_N, showing it is a weighted sum of canonical averages across different N.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Bridges the two ensemble expressions; without this step the equivalence argument has no foundation.

items.title: Thermodynamic limit and density
items.description: The response states that the two averages coincide only in the thermodynamic limit N, V → ∞ with the density N/V held fixed.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Equivalence at finite N' (severity high); verified_findings confirm the fixed-density condition is absent from the reference but present in correct rollouts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims grand-canonical and canonical averages coincide at finite N without the thermodynamic limit.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on [reference, rollout_1, negative_constructed1]: reference=false, negative_constructed1=true

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core condition from the reference answer; absorbs the finite-N avoidance since both resolve identically.

validation.gold_why: States coincidence occurs in the thermodynamic limit.

items.title: No long-range interactions
items.description: The response states that ensemble equivalence requires systems without long-range interactions.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly from the reference answer; correctness collapses if this condition is absent.

items.title: Away from phase transitions
items.description: The response states that ensemble equivalence holds only when the system is not near phase transitions or critical points.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Second key condition from the reference answer; distinguishing valid from invalid regimes.

items.title: Fluctuation scaling 1/√V
items.description: The response writes the relative particle-number fluctuation as (⟨N²⟩ − ⟨N⟩²)^{1/2}/⟨N⟩ and states it scales as 1/√V, vanishing in the thermodynamic limit so that the ensembles become equivalent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong fluctuation scaling' (severity low); consensus_correct in agreement_analysis confirms all rollouts state ΔN/⟨N⟩ ~ 1/√V → 0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states relative fluctuations vanish as 1/N rather than 1/√V, or that does not state how fluctuations vanish.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on [reference, rollout_1, negative_constructed1]: reference=false, negative_constructed1=false; validation table confirms n_negatives_failed=2

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; gold=FAIL but the scaling argument is the mechanistic reason for equivalence.

validation.gold_why: No fluctuation scaling discussed.

items.title: μ controls particle number
items.description: The response states that increasing the chemical potential μ increases the average particle number in the grand canonical ensemble.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to consider the role of chemical potential; this physical interpretation underpins the density-tuning condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats μ as a free parameter without connecting it to the particle number or density control in the grand canonical ensemble.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on [reference, negative_constructed1]: reference=false, negative_constructed1=false; validation table confirms n_negatives_failed=2

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; gold=FAIL but this establishes the role of μ in matching ensembles.

validation.gold_why: No mention of μ controlling particle number.

items.title: μ tuned to match density
items.description: The response states that the chemical potential μ is adjusted so that the grand canonical average density ⟨N⟩_GC/V equals the canonical density N/V, making the two ensembles describe the same physical system.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects μ to density as the question requests; without this the role of chemical potential is incomplete.

items.title: Equivalence statement
items.description: The response states that the grand canonical averages converge to the canonical averages, ⟨A⟩_GC → ⟨A⟩_C, as V → ∞ when density and temperature are held equal between the two ensembles.

provenance.calibration_rationale: The central conclusion the question asks for; without it the response does not answer the question.

items.title: Canonical partition function
items.description: The response writes the canonical partition function as Z_N = Σ_i e^{−βE_i} or Z_N = Tr_N(e^{−βH}) for a system of N particles at fixed volume.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Supporting definition that grounds the canonical average; adds depth but is not the main point.

items.title: Fixed vs fluctuating N
items.description: The response states that particle number N is fixed in the canonical ensemble and fluctuates in the grand canonical ensemble, and that the equivalence rests on these fluctuations becoming negligible.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Frames why the two ensembles differ and why the thermodynamic limit resolves the difference.

items.title: Grand canonical P(N)
items.description: The response states that the probability of N particles in the grand canonical ensemble is P(N) = Z_N e^{βμN}/Ξ, which becomes sharply peaked around ⟨N⟩ for large V.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate result explaining why fluctuations vanish; real depth but beyond the minimum required.

items.title: Avoids wrong 1/V scaling
items.description: Avoids stating that relative particle-number fluctuations vanish as 1/V rather than 1/√V in the thermodynamic limit.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific wrong scaling exponent; naming 1/V as the incorrect value keeps the trap checkable.

items.title: Directionality 3′–5′
items.description: States "3′ to 5′" as the directionality of the exonuclease proofreading activity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong directionality' (severity high); counterexample with 5′→3′ was verified_incorrect=true and confirmed to fail the 3′→5′ check.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists both 3′ to 5′ and 5′ to 3′ exonuclease as proofreading, or reverses the direction to 5′ to 3′, fails this criterion.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion batch 1 confirmed counterexample_numeric_error states 5′→3′, not 3′→5′; verified_evidence also confirms this counterexample is verified_incorrect

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core component of the correct answer; gold=pass. Discrimination low but fact is indispensable.

validation.gold_why: States 3′ to 5′, not 5′ to 3′.

items.title: Exonuclease type
items.description: Identifies the proofreading activity as exonuclease activity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exonuclease vs endonuclease' (severity medium); proofreading removes the terminal mispaired nucleotide, which is exonucleolytic, not endonucleolytic.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says "3′ to 5′ endonuclease activity of DNA polymerase δ" fails this criterion.

tool_critic.evidence: Not directly tested; no endonuclease counterexample was constructed or run

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing for correctness; gold=pass. Absorbs endonuclease-avoidance source 9.

validation.gold_why: Says exonuclease, not endonuclease.

items.title: DNA polymerase δ
items.description: Names DNA polymerase δ as the enzyme performing this proofreading activity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Naming polymerase α' (severity medium); counterexample with DNA polymerase α was verified_incorrect=true because Pol α lacks 3′→5′ proofreading exonuclease.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes proofreading to DNA polymerase α (primase) instead of δ fails this criterion.

tool_critic.evidence: verified_evidence confirms Pol α counterexample verified_incorrect=true; execute_criterion batch 1 showed this counterexample failing criterion 2 (which requires Pol δ)

provenance.calibration_rationale: Indispensable enzyme identification; gold=pass. Absorbs avoidance of α, primase, RNA pol.

validation.gold_why: No mention of polymerase α.

items.title: Avoids polymerase ε
items.description: Avoids including DNA polymerase ε alongside DNA polymerase δ as a co-equal answer for this proofreading activity.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three independent rollouts named both δ and ε, while the reference names only δ; this was the sole point of universal disagreement between attempts and the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states "3′ to 5′ exonuclease activity of DNA polymerase δ and DNA polymerase ε" fails this criterion while a δ-only response passes.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion batch 2: reference passes, all three rollouts fail

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives—sole proven discriminator. Observed shared error, high weight warranted.

validation.gold_why: No mention of polymerase ε.

items.title: Proofreading vs MMR
items.description: Distinguishes this 3′ to 5′ exonuclease proofreading from post-replicative mismatch repair (MMR) proteins (e.g., MSH2, MLH1) as the mechanism determining the base substitution mutation rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Confusing with mismatch repair' (severity high); counterexample_wrong_principle using MMR was verified_incorrect=true.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes the MMR pathway for intrinsic polymerase proofreading fails this criterion even if it mentions mutation rate.

tool_critic.evidence: verified_evidence confirms MMR counterexample verified_incorrect=true; make_counterexample re-registered counterexample_wrong_principle as MMR-based but execute_criterion timed out before re-testing

provenance.calibration_rationale: Genuine conceptual distinction for this question; gold=pass. Caught 0/3 but not a near-duplicate.

validation.gold_why: No MMR proteins mentioned.

items.title: During synthesis
items.description: States that the proofreading activity occurs during DNA replication.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question_structure's implicit constraints state the activity must be directly part of the nuclear DNA replication machinery, not a post-replicative repair pathway.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly names the exonuclease activity and DNA polymerase δ but describes it as occurring after replication fails this criterion.

tool_critic.evidence: Not directly tested; the re-made MMR counterexample uses post-synthetic framing and might trigger this, but execute_criterion timed out

provenance.calibration_rationale: Real temporal distinction implied by the question; gold=pass. Low discrimination but distinct.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Specifies that the proofreading activity occurs in nuclear DNA replication.

validation.gold_why: No post-replicative framing stated.

items.title: Human context
items.description: Specifies that the proofreading activity occurs in human chromosomes.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Bacterial polymerase swap' (severity medium); the question specifies human chromosomes, so a bacterial enzyme is contextually wrong.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names DNA polymerase III as the proofreading enzyme for human nuclear replication fails this criterion.

tool_critic.evidence: Not directly tested; no bacterial-enzyme counterexample was constructed or run

provenance.calibration_rationale: Question anchor for human context; gold=pass. Absorbs bacterial-polymerase-III avoidance.

validation.gold_why: No bacterial enzyme mentioned.

provenance.evidence_detail: Verified finding: counterexample attributing the blue precipitate to Fe³⁺ was verified INCORRECT; the ferricyanide test detects Fe²⁺, not Fe³⁺.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the blue precipitate with potassium ferricyanide to Fe³⁺ (ferric ions) instead of Fe²⁺ (ferrous ions).

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion against reference: FAILS (equation-only); candidate validation shows discrimination 0.5 — constructed1 fails it; verified_evidence confirms wrong answer attributing precipitate to Fe

provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference answer specifies this exact equation; shares 0.5 discrimination from source candidate 5.

validation.gold_why: Equation shows Fe²⁺ reacting with ferricyanide.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Required diagnostic for the Fe³⁺ impurity; question-grounded but not separately validated.

items.title: Intron addition as mechanism
items.description: States that the addition of introns is a distinct mechanism by which the DNA strand changes through generations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent analysis shows rollouts 1 and 2 discuss intron gain/loss only within a subsection, while only rollout 3 and the reference elevate addition of introns to a top-level mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions introns only in the context of their functions but never frames the addition of introns as a mechanism of DNA change across generations.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on reference + negatives (all pass) and on rollouts (rollout_2 fails)

provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=0.50; intron addition is the most distinctive mechanism in the reference.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: States that mutations are a mechanism by which the DNA strand changes through generations.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states addition of introns as a mechanism.

items.title: Chromosome number changes
items.description: States that changes in chromosome number are a mechanism of DNA change through generations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent analysis shows all three rollouts decompose chromosome-level changes into sub-types (rearrangements, fusions, polyploidy) rather than using the reference's umbrella framing of changes in chromosome number.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists chromosomal rearrangements and gene duplication without identifying changes in chromosome number as a distinct mechanism.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on reference, negative_constructed1, negative_constructed2, and rollouts 1–3: all pass

provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=0.50; one of three named mechanisms in the reference answer.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly names changes in chromosome number.

items.title: Mechanism-to-complexity link
items.description: States that the mechanisms of DNA change, including intron addition, mutations, or changes in chromosome number, can affect the complexity of the DNA.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'unlinked complexity claim' notes the temptation to list mechanisms without stating how they affect complexity, leaving sub-question (b) unanswered.
provenance.discriminates: A response that catalogues mechanisms (introns, mutations, chromosome changes) but never states how any of them affect the complexity of the DNA.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on reference + negatives: reference fails, negative_constructed2 passes

provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=0.50 but gold=FAIL; kept low because reference did not visibly satisfy it.

validation.gold_why: Says mechanisms affect complexity but no specific links per mechanism.

items.title: Avoid over-enumerating mechanisms
items.description: Avoids listing seven or more separate mechanisms of DNA change without identifying the addition of introns, mutations, and changes in chromosome number among them.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'over-enumerating mechanisms' (severity: high, observed: reference_contrast) notes all rollouts list 7–10 mechanisms, burying the core three the reference names.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists point mutations, gene duplication, transposons, exon shuffling, HGT, repeat expansion, recombination, and chromosomal rearrangements without highlighting addition of introns, mutations, and changes in chromosome number as the central mechanisms.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on rollouts: all three rollouts (presumably correct) fail, while reference and one negative pass

provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=0.50; catches responses that pad with mechanisms while missing core ones.

validation.gold_why: Lists only three mechanisms, does not over-enumerate.

items.title: Avoid C-value paradox claim
items.description: Avoids claiming that more DNA always directly increases complexity, ignoring that complexity depends on gene number, alternative splicing, and regulatory capacity rather than raw DNA amount.

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on reference, negative_constructed1, negative_constructed2, and rollouts 1–3: all pass

validation.gold_why: Does not claim more DNA always increases complexity.

items.title: H₂C=O unshared pair
items.description: Lists H₂C=O under base category (a)(2) molecules with an unshared pair of electrons, treating the base categories as non-exclusive.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts omit H₂C=O from (a)(2), placing it only in (a)(3); the reference answer includes it in both categories.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the four base categories as mutually exclusive and places H₂C=O only under (a)(3).

tool_critic.evidence: execute_criterion on reference (true), rollout_1/2/3 (all false), and negative_constructed1/negative_rollout1/negative_rollout2 (all false)

provenance.calibration_rationale: Proven 1.00 discrimination (caught 3/3 negatives); central shared error.

validation.gold_why: H₂C=O listed under (a)(2).

items.title: H₂C=O π dipole
items.description: Lists H₂C=O under base category (a)(3) negative end of a π bond dipole.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Requires π-bond-dipole understanding; no measured discrimination but key reasoning.

items.title: Ethene π electrons
items.description: Lists H₂C=CH₂ under base category (a)(4) available π electrons rather than under (a)(2) molecules with an unshared pair of electrons.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined low-severity pitfall 'Ethene π-electrons missed': the π electrons of ethene may be confused with unshared lone pairs.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists ethene under molecules with an unshared pair because π electrons are perceived as available electrons.

tool_critic.evidence: candidate description not visible; could not test

provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed avoidance of lone-pair misclassification; names specific wrong move.

validation.gold_why: Ethene placed under (a)(4), not (a)(2).

items.title: BF₃ electron-deficient
items.description: Lists BF₃ under acid category (b)(2) species with electron-deficient atoms, not under (b)(3) species with an atom capable of expanding an octet.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined medium-severity pitfall 'BF₃ vs SiF₄ misclassified': boron has an incomplete octet, not an expandable one.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places BF₃ under expanding an octet because it accepts an electron pair, confusing an incomplete octet with an expandable one.

tool_critic.evidence: candidate description not visible; could not test

provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed avoidance of octet-expansion misclassification; no measured discrimination.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Lists SiF₄ under acid category (b)(3) species with an atom capable of expanding an octet, not under (b)(2) species with electron-deficient atoms.

validation.gold_why: BF₃ not placed under (b)(3).

items.title: CO₂ positive end
items.description: Lists :O=C=O: under acid category (b)(4) positive end of a π bond dipole, identifying the central carbon as the positive end rather than the oxygen atoms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined medium-severity pitfall 'CO₂ π-dipole direction reversed': oxygen is more electronegative, so one might instinctively place the reactive site at oxygen rather than the electrophilic carbon.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reverses the π bond dipole direction in CO₂, identifying oxygen as the electron-poor positive end.

tool_critic.evidence: candidate description not visible; could not test

provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbed avoidance of oxygen-as-positive-end error; requires π-dipole reasoning.

validation.gold_why: CO₂ carbon identified as positive end via (b)(4).
